chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: “A man was the executor of another man, then he died and appointed another man as executor. Is the executor bound by the bequest of the man whose executor this one had been?”
So he عليه السلام wrote: “It is binding upon him according to his right, if there is a due right for him against him, if Allah wills.”

key_terms.الْوَصِيَّ: the executor who bears legal responsibility
key_terms.بِحَقِّهِ: in accordance with his established right
key_terms.حَقٌّ: a valid legal claim or due right
key_terms.وَأَوْصَى: he appointed by will or testament
key_terms.وَصِيَّ: executor or trustee appointed over a bequest

ai.seo_question: Is the executor of an executor required to carry out the original bequest in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal responsibility of a successor-executor when the original executor dies after appointing another in his place. Imam al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام states that the obligation applies in accordance with an established right or claim, indicating that the duty is tied to valid legal entitlement.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5535 - Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, wrote to Abu Muhammad Imam Hasan ibn Ali Al-Askari (as), asking:
"A man was the executor of another man's will, and then he died and appointed another man as his executor. Is the second executor obligated to fulfill the will of the man for whom the first executor was appointed?"
Imam (as) wrote in response: "He is obligated by his right if there is a rightful claim upon him, if Allah (swt) wills."
